ISAAC MUTE
Allotment
DISMISSED
ORDER
The appellant previously appealed from a decision of the
Anchorage office of the Bureau of Land Management informing him
that his allotment application would be subject to an o il and gas
reservation to the United States. By our decision of May 22, 1972
we remanded the record to permit the appellant to select
afforded by section 18(a) of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement
Act of December 18, 1971, P.L. 92-203. He has elected to pursue
his application for a Native allotment under the Act of May 17,
1906. He has requested consideration of his appeal — concerning
whether his allotment is subject to an o il and gas reservation.
In Anna A. 7 IBLA 323, 79 (1972) we held that
appeals from Bureau of Land Management decisions which are not dis
positive of the ultimate issues will not be considered. As we said
in
The primary question before the Bureau of Land
Management is the appellant's entitlement to an allot
ment. Only if an allotment is approved will it be
necessary to inquire whether it should be subject to
a mineral reservation in favor of the United States.
Any consideration of a mineral reservation requirement
prior to the determination of the primary question is pre
mature. In such case the appeal is properly dismissed
without prejudice.
Therefore, pursuant to the authority delegated to the Board of
Land Appeals, 43 CFR 4.1, the appeal is dismissed. The case record
is for appropriate processing; if the appellant is entitled
to an allotment he will then be informed relative to the mineral

( (
IBLA
classification of the land and afforded an opportunity to disprove
or appeal if a mineral reservation is required.
